$comment: SYNTHETIC, and the fixture that proves the enumeration is CLOSED. DL-105 accepts three known lorastats dialects and rule 4 says an unknown FOURTH still dead-letters: 'all the known dialects' is exactly three, and a union allowed to grow silently is a contract nobody understands - the half of DL-089 that still stands after Q15a. This record is a plausible fourth spelling (lorawan_ rather than lora_) carrying version:1 like every other dialect, so nothing on it announces that it is new. It matches none of the three oneOf branches: dialects A and B require BARE required names, dialect C requires lora_-prefixed ones. It passes the ENVELOPE, so Input returns 200 and publishes - the disagreement is the Writer's to surface, not a 400 Heimdal would never retry (ADR-007 §5). If this fixture ever starts validating, the enumeration has been reopened; a DLQ spike is never resolved by widening the schema to make it stop. DL-105 widened it because ZC explained the dialects, not because the queue was full. NOTE: tenant and maintenant deliberately DIFFER here, unlike the byte-faithful production fixtures.
